sets.title: Access guard with no feature flag noise (control)
sets.description: The authorize method in three policy classes, all pristine. Carrier A, B, and C are all identical (no feature flag guard noise inserted). This is the control set for K-22: tools should detect all three as clones without any feature flag noise present.
sets.notes: Control set for K-22 (nz_flag). All three carriers are pristine — no feature flag guard noise. Detectors should find all three members with high confidence.

capability_probe.pass_criterion: Tool correctly pairs all 3 carriers despite presence of feature flag guard noise
capability_probe.fail_meaning: Tool cannot filter out feature flag noise; reports no pair or missed clone between noisy carriers

distractors.reason: near-miss: same auth vocabulary but computes numeric trust score instead of boolean decision

sets.title: Access guard with feature flag guard noise
sets.description: The authorize method in three policy classes. Carrier A is pristine; carrier B wraps the body in if ($this->flags->enabled('v2')) { ... } (NZ-06); carrier C wraps at a different point. The feature flag guard (NZ-06) is noise that should be filtered. This tests whether tools can see through feature flag wrappers to detect the underlying clone. Requires noise_filtering + cfg_comparison capabilities.
sets.notes: Probe set for K-22 (nz_flag). Uses NZ-06 (feature_flag) transform to insert if (!getenv('FEATURE_ENABLED')) { return null; } after last statement in method body. Carrier C uses a different flag name. K-22 requires noise_filtering + cfg_comparison: tools must see through the feature flag wrapper to detect the underlying clone. Note: The spec calls for $this->flags->enabled('v2') but the existing NZ-06 transform uses getenv(). Using the transform as-is for the test corpus.
